title: Garry Tan's Claude Code Plan-Mode prompt
blurb: The Y Combinator CEO's review prompt: opinionated tradeoffs, four review lenses, and a structured interaction protocol.
body:
Garry Tan (CEO, Y Combinator) shared his Claude Code prompt for Plan Mode — a structured code-review template.

Engineering preferences (the guardrails)

  • DRY is important — flag repetition aggressively
  • Well-tested code is non-negotiable; rather too many tests than too few
  • "Engineered enough" — not fragile/hacky, not over-abstracted
  • Err on handling more edge cases, not fewer; thoughtfulness > speed
  • Bias toward explicit over clever

Four review lenses

1. Architecture (system design, coupling, bottlenecks, security) · 2. Code quality (organization, DRY, error handling, tech debt) · 3. Tests (coverage gaps, assertion strength, edge cases) · 4. Performance (N+1 queries, memory, caching).

Interaction protocol

For each issue: describe it concretely with file/line; present 2–3 options (including "do nothing"); give a recommended option mapped to the preferences; then explicitly ask before proceeding. Number issues, letter the options, make the recommended option first.

SOURCE · Garry Tan, shared by Paolo Perrone (ML Engineer).
